rationale: NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching, and Spectrum-6 landed named first customers including CoreWeave, Microsoft, Nebius, SpaceXAI and Tesla, with photonics claimed at five times better power efficiency across 100,000-GPU deployments.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open Ethernet alternatives winning large clusters on price.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: When each answer costs less to produce, buyers run far more of them, so cheaper compute grows total chip demand instead of shrinking it.
rationale: Open-source inference costs have fallen 30-50% a year with token prices dropping far faster on some measures, NVIDIA claims an order-of-magnitude lower cost per token with NVLink systems, and AT&T is now burning about a trillion tokens a month.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether falling prices per token keep converting into higher total token volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Buyers who put cash down years ahead for memory have already paid for the accelerators that memory goes into, so that demand is committed rather than hoped for.
rationale: Micron holds 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay deals backed by over $22B including nearly $18B of cash deposits, and HBM suppliers have sold out 2026 output under non-cancellable contracts with hyperscalers locking multi-year supply.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any large depositor walks away and forfeits its prepayment.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Licenses only turn into sales if buyers, tariffs and inventory all line up, and right now they do not, so a paper reopening delivers no revenue.
rationale: The licensing door is open on paper - roughly ten Chinese firms cleared for up to 75,000 chips each and about $10B of approved licenses - but actual shipments stay trivial, no revenue has been booked, a 25% tariff applies, Blackwell is still banned, and enforcement raids are widening.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the first real H200 shipments actually clear customs and book revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Customers stay on NVIDIA when porting their software is painful, and each rival software release that closes the gap lowers that cost of leaving.
rationale: AMD's software stack posted 3.3x inference and 2.4x training gains over its prior release and a 2.10x throughput jump on a leading open model, while Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Oracle and Rackspace committed to Instinct in production, so software is less of a barrier than before.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced rival deployments actually run production workloads at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Memory is a big share of an AI server's bill of materials, so sharp memory price rises push up the cost of every rack and squeeze whoever cannot pass it on.
rationale: Server memory contract prices are set to rise more than 25% in one quarter, DRAM lead times stretch to 32-40 weeks with prices up about 90% since late 2025, AI-server rack component costs are inflating 2-3% a week, and AMD is raising Radeon bundle prices about 10% on memory costs.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new memory fab capacity arriving from late 2026 relieves prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Several vendors reach volume production in the same half, so total accelerator units available to buyers steps up at once.
rationale: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin enters production ramp in the third quarter, AMD's Helios reached full production with shipments starting the same quarter, and next-generation parts from AWS and Google are moving to mass production together, though AMD's rack-scale volume ramp slips toward 2027.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to packaging and memory allocation, which can hold back a ramp even when the chip is ready.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD customerConcentration eases as its buyer base broadens over the next two quarters.
mechanism: A few enormous contracts carry nearly all of the growth, so one partner delaying or cancelling swings AMD's data-center line hard.
rationale: AMD's pipeline is a short list of very large commitments - Anthropic at 2 gigawatts, OpenAI at 6 gigawatts, Meta at up to 6 gigawatts, Microsoft and Oracle - and AMD itself says it expects continued customer concentration, with an equity investment tying one of those buyers to it.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether smaller enterprise and cloud buyers pick up Instinct in volume.

falsifiableTrigger: Crescent Island releaseCadence slips its customer sampling past the 2H 2026 quarter.
mechanism: Using ordinary memory instead of stacked memory removes the advanced-packaging step that gates everyone else, so this chip can be built with capacity that is not fought over.
rationale: Intel's Crescent Island still targets second-half 2026 customer sampling using up to 480GB of standard LPDDR5X rather than high-bandwidth memory, explicitly to avoid packaging and memory contention.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the lower memory bandwidth is good enough for real inference jobs.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: When many kinds of chips chase the same fab and packaging slots, the foundry can choose the best-paying work and lift prices.
rationale: TSMC posted a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, raised full-year growth guidance to above 40% and lifted capex to $60-64B, while demand spreading into ASICs, networking and power chips tightens capacity across nodes and packaging.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a slowdown in AI orders that would leave newly added capacity underused.

falsifiableTrigger: A hyperscalerCapexRevision cuts 2026 or 2027 AI capex guidance within two quarters.
mechanism: If the money spent on AI capacity does not come back as revenue, buyers cut orders, but cloud revenue and profit are so far rising alongside the spending.
rationale: Rather than pulling back, Alphabet raised 2026 capex to $195-205B for a second time and reported cloud revenue up 82% with operating income at $8.8B, CoreWeave roughly doubled its capex plan, and the four largest buyers track toward about $725B; only market jitters and analyst worry point the other way.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to cloud revenue growth stalling while capex commitments stay locked in.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA grossMargin guidance drops below 70% in a coming quarter.
mechanism: Buyers keep paying premium prices because supply is short and alternatives are limited, so margin holds even through a costly product transition.
rationale: NVIDIA reported a 75.0% non-GAAP gross margin and guided the next quarter to the same level, far above AMD at 55% guided to 56% and Intel in the low 40s.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory cost inflation and the cost of ramping the next generation.

falsifiableTrigger: Top-buyer customerConcentration in CoWoS output falls below 85% within a year.
mechanism: A very small number of buyers fill the packaging lines, so if one cuts orders there is no queue of other customers ready to take the slots.
rationale: The top three packaging customers still take more than 85% of TSMC output, with NVIDIA at about 60% and AMD about 11%, and AMD must split its slice between server processors and accelerators.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether custom-chip and networking customers grow into meaningful packaging buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: Aggregate rpoBacklog duration shortens as new commitments turn shorter-dated over two quarters.
mechanism: Buyers who fear being short of compute sign longer contracts, so the order book stretches further into the future than the delivery schedule.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog jumped more than $50B in a quarter to $514B with only just over half converting within 24 months, CoreWeave's backlog reached $99.4B including a Meta commitment running to 2032, and Micron's take-or-pay deals run five years.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new bookings keep their long tenor as capacity loosens.

falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports revenue (apiArr) growth stalling quarter over quarter while compute commitments keep growing.
mechanism: Model providers pay for compute out of subscription and interface sales, so rising sales make their compute commitments look funded rather than speculative.
rationale: Anthropic's annual run-rate revenue passed $30B in April 2026 from $1B in January 2025, its models are in production on Azure, and it has signed multi-gigawatt compute deals it says are needed to meet customer demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether model-provider revenue growth keeps pace with commitments that now run into the tens of billions.

falsifiableTrigger: Chinese domestic accelerator designWins for frontier training stall over the next two quarters.
mechanism: Once local chips can train a frontier model, buyers blocked from imports have a working substitute and stop queuing for licensed foreign parts.
rationale: Meituan trained a 1.6-trillion-parameter model on more than 50,000 domestic accelerators with no NVIDIA chips across 35 trillion tokens, and Chinese labs are commissioning their own inference chips, though viable in-house silicon is judged more than two years out.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply and software maturity on the domestic stack.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt load or net loss narrows for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buying GPU fleets on credit means interest and depreciation grow faster than rental revenue, so sales records come with bigger losses.
rationale: CoreWeave's revenue grew about 168% to $5.1B while its net loss widened from $937M to $1.2B, even as it raised 2026 capex to $31-35B.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental prices, which decide whether the fleet ever earns back its cost.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler cuts its 2027 gigawatt power target below its 2026 level.
mechanism: A site can only run as many accelerators as it has electricity and electrical gear for, so power and transformers now set the ceiling on deployments.
rationale: Buildouts are now sized in gigawatts - Meta at 7 gigawatts in 2026 and roughly double in 2027, AMD deals quoted at 2 and 6 gigawatts - while Gartner expects 40% of AI data centers to be power-constrained by 2027 and transformer lead times average 128 weeks.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection timing and transformer delivery, which move slower than chip supply.

falsifiableTrigger: Broadcom-plus-Marvell market-share-pct of custom ASIC co-design falls below 90% within a year.
mechanism: Custom chips still mostly go through two design partners, so their capacity and pricing gate the alternative to merchant GPUs unless new partners appear.
rationale: Broadcom and Marvell still hold an estimated 95% of custom AI chip co-design, but Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung to build a custom chip on a 2nm process and Chinese labs are pursuing their own designs, so the two-house channel is starting to face alternatives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new design partners such as Samsung convert early talks into shipping silicon.

falsifiableTrigger: Wistron odmMonthlyAiRevenue falls year-over-year for two consecutive months.
mechanism: Contract manufacturers only bill when finished servers leave the factory, so their monthly revenue is a direct check that orders are turning into hardware.
rationale: Wistron posted record June 2026 revenue of NT$321.82B, up 53.9% year over year and 10.9% month over month on AI-server and networking shipments, with supply-chain players reporting an order boom into the second half.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to component shortages that can hold finished racks in the factory.

falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's marginalBuyerFinancing debt-to-equity rises above 6:1 within two quarters.
mechanism: GPU fleets are bought with borrowed money secured on the chips, so a thin equity cushion leaves little room if rental income or resale values fall.
rationale: CoreWeave has raised $18.81B of debt against $3.5B of equity, a 5.4 to 1 ratio, with total debt of $24.86B up 16.1% in a single quarter, while it doubles capex plans.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to how lenders value used accelerators as collateral.

falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics adoption stalls below 5% of AI optical modules through 2027.
mechanism: Putting the optics into the switch package cuts power per link, so cluster wiring gets tied to a new and narrow set of packaging suppliers.
rationale: Co-packaged optics is set to climb from about 0.5% of AI optical modules in 2026 to roughly 35% by 2030, NVIDIA's photonics switches ship this year with named first customers, and Taiwanese packaging houses are newly competing for silicon photonics work.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield and serviceability of packaged optics in live clusters.

falsifiableTrigger: A named US fab or packaging project slips its build milestone past 2027.
mechanism: Vendors are funding fabs and packaging lines outside Taiwan, which adds a second place these parts can be made if the first is disrupted.
rationale: NVIDIA plans up to $500B of US-built AI infrastructure with TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron and Amkor; Micron committed $250B to US memory manufacturing through 2035 and broke ground in New York on July 9, 2026; Intel added EUR 5B of capacity and grew foundry revenue 31%.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction and qualification timelines, since announcements run years ahead of output.

falsifiableTrigger: Google Cloud or CoreWeave rpoBacklog fails to grow sequentially for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Cloud sellers sign contracts faster than they can build capacity, so the unshipped order book grows and shows demand earlier than the revenue line does.
rationale: Google Cloud's backlog grew more than $50B sequentially to $514B with just over half due to convert within 24 months while cloud revenue accelerated to 82% growth, and CoreWeave's backlog climbed to $99.4B from $66.8B a month earlier.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether booked contracts actually convert to revenue on schedule.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Spending has outgrown what operating cash can cover, so buyers raise debt and equity to keep building, which links future orders to open capital markets.
rationale: Alphabet funded its June-quarter buildout with $49.6B of equity issuance and $20.3B of notes and reported its first ever negative free cash flow of $5.9B, while NVIDIA raised $25B of bonds to finance customer purchases and CoreWeave keeps leveraging up.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and investor appetite for financing AI capacity.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Each generation does more work for the same electricity, so a site with a fixed power budget can buy more useful compute without new grid capacity.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest systems are stated at up to 10 times the performance per megawatt of the gear they replace, its photonics networking claims five times better power efficiency, and the prior generation step measured about 1.6 times better performance per watt.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor efficiency claims hold up in real deployments rather than benchmarks.

detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast new memory capacity from the three suppliers converts into shipped stacks.

detail.mechanism: Scarce memory lets suppliers set the price, so a larger slice of what a buyer pays for an AI server ends up as memory-maker profit.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory fabs coming online and restoring buyer bargaining power.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.

detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to public funding decisions and to whether these projects secure power and packaging allocation.
detail.statement: National projects and large enterprises are now placing accelerator orders big enough to matter alongside the cloud giants.

detail.statement: Intel's data-center and foundry businesses are growing again with better margins, adding a third source of AI-adjacent supply.

falsifiableTrigger: B200 rpoBacklog falls below 2 million units for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Buyers place multi-year orders faster than memory and packaging suppliers can build the parts NVIDIA needs to fill them.
rationale: NVIDIA data-center revenue hit a record $75.2B up 92% year over year, B200 orders reached about 3.6 million units, and memory and packaging remain sold out, so orders keep running ahead of what NVIDIA can ship.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging supply loosening enough to clear the order book.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes ease to available-on-demand and CoWoS lead times fall below 26 weeks before the end of 2027.
mechanism: Every accelerator needs both stacked memory and advanced packaging, so whichever is scarcer sets the ceiling on total shipments.
note: supply-constraint-binding: deferred: secondary-only reversal (2 distinct publishers < 3)
rationale: Stacked memory is sold out through 2026 and much of 2027, TSMC packaging carries 52 to 78 week waits and is booked into 2027, even as packaging capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month, so both limits still cap shipments.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging capacity additions arriving faster than demand.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD accelerator market-share-pct fails to rise above 7% through 2027.
mechanism: Large multi-year customer commitments feed later shipments that show up as datacenter accelerator share gains.
rationale: AMD still holds only about 5 to 7 percent share, but gigawatt-scale wins with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Oracle plus data-center revenue up 57 percent point to that share converting soon.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments turn into shipped and recognized revenue.

falsifiableTrigger: ASIC market-share-pct growth falls back below GPU growth for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Hyperscalers move inference work onto their own cheaper chips, taking growth that would otherwise go to merchant GPUs.
rationale: Custom chips are set to grow about 45 percent in 2026 versus 16 percent for merchant GPUs, custom silicon already covers a large slice of total compute, and Meta is putting new in-house accelerators into production.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether captive custom chips can match merchant GPU software and performance at scale.

falsifiableTrigger: gpuSpotPrice for H100 or GB200 drops more than 20% within a quarter.
mechanism: Tight supply keeps rental demand above available capacity, so hourly prices stay firm.
rationale: Rental prices are holding, with H100 up about 24 percent from its late-2025 low and current cloud rates steady, even as more supply arrives.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a fast supply ramp arriving before demand absorbs it.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure eases so China DC revenue recovers above prior levels within two quarters.
mechanism: License rules block or delay the chips Chinese buyers want, removing that revenue from the served market.
rationale: NVIDIA's China revenue fell by more than half to $4.55B with no Hopper shipments, H200 sales stayed trivial, and the top chip's export stayed banned, so policy is cutting real addressable demand.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to US and China policy shifts on which chips may ship.

falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed GPU commitments in rpoBacklog exceed 300,000 units within two quarters.
mechanism: NVIDIA funds the buyers who then order its chips, so its own credit props up part of its reported demand.
rationale: NVIDIA scaled a revenue-sharing and backstop program covering about 210,000 GPUs across Firmus and Sharon AI and issued $25B of bonds, so more reported demand rests on NVIDIA-extended credit.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how large the vendor-financed share of orders grows relative to cash-funded orders.

falsifiableTrigger: customerConcentration for the top three direct customers falls below prior shares next fiscal year.
mechanism: A few large buyers place most orders, so any one slowing or moving to in-house chips would dent demand sharply.
rationale: Three direct customers were 21, 17 and 16 percent of NVIDIA's revenue and the top four were more than half, so concentration stays high.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a single top hyperscaler cutting orders or switching to its own silicon.

falsifiableTrigger: NVIDIA DC Ethernet switch market-share-pct slips from #1 within two quarters.
mechanism: Selling networking together with GPUs makes the full system harder to swap out for standalone chips.
rationale: NVIDIA became the revenue leader in datacenter Ethernet switches for the first time and is shipping new Spectrum networking with marquee cloud customers, deepening the bundled-system tie.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to open networking standards letting buyers mix rival switches with any accelerator.

falsifiableTrigger: Cost-per-token gains stall so tokenEconomics improves less than one generation cycle.
mechanism: Lower cost per token makes more AI use cases affordable, expanding the work that runs on NVIDIA GPUs.
rationale: NVIDIA's newest generation cut inference cost per token about tenfold, and open-source inference costs keep falling fast, pulling more workloads onto its chips.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each new generation keeps cutting cost per token.

falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid HBM commitments in rpoBacklog shrink or deposits are refunded within a quarter.
mechanism: Binding prepaid contracts commit buyers to take the memory and chips regardless of later conditions.
rationale: Micron signed 16 non-cancelable five-year take-or-pay memory deals backed by more than $22B, and NVIDIA lifted total prepaid supply commitments toward $145B, locking future accelerator demand in place.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether customers can walk away from or renegotiate the prepaid deals.

falsifiableTrigger: exportControlExposure changes lift the sub-50% China cap or clear Blackwell within two quarters.
mechanism: Case-by-case licenses and a hard cap let only a trickle of chips through while the best parts stay blocked.
rationale: China access stayed limited to case-by-case H200-class licenses under a sub-50 percent cap with only about ten cleared buyers and the top chip still banned, matching the capped-reopening picture.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to policy moves that raise the cap or approve the banned top-tier chip.

falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: As rival software matures and cuts cost, customers can move workloads off NVIDIA despite the switching effort.
rationale: AMD posted large inference and training software gains, won production commitments from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta, and showed a lower total cost of ownership than NVIDIA, so the software lock-in is holding customers less tightly than before.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast rival software stacks close the ease-of-use gap with CUDA.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory hbmSupplyCapex expansion pulls DRAM/NVMe prices down within two quarters.
mechanism: Scarce memory and storage bid up prices for the parts that make up most of an AI server's bill of materials.
rationale: AI-server rack component costs are climbing 2 to 3 percent a week, standard memory prices jumped roughly 90 percent, spot DDR4 rose over 17 percent in a month, and stacked-memory contract prices are set to double.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and easing prices.

falsifiableTrigger: releaseCadence slips push a major vendor's 2H-2026 ramp into 2027.
mechanism: Several vendors ramping new accelerators at once adds to the total pool of available compute.
rationale: NVIDIA Vera Rubin, AMD Helios, AWS Trainium3 and Google TPU are all lined up for mass production in the second half of 2026, though AMD's next rack part slipped its full ramp toward 2027.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether any one mega-customer delays or cancels.

rationale: Intel's Crescent Island stayed on track to sample in the second half of 2026 using standard LPDDR5X memory up to 480GB, sidestepping the packaging and stacked-memory crunch.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether standard-memory parts deliver enough performance to attract buyers.

falsifiableTrigger: TSMC grossMargin declines for two consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
mechanism: AI demand across many chip types keeps TSMC's lines full, giving it room to raise prices.
rationale: TSMC's gross margin rose more than 9 points to about 68 percent with packaging sold out and lead times stretched, showing broad AI demand filling capacity and lifting prices.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to a broad AI demand slowdown that frees up capacity.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to competition or rising memory and packaging costs squeezing margins.

sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction timelines and whether the pledged projects actually break ground.

rationale: Google Cloud's backlog grew $50B in a quarter to $514B and CoreWeave's rose from about $67B to $99B, showing cloud providers booking compute far faster than they can deliver.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new bookings keep outpacing deliveries.

falsifiableTrigger: A top hyperscaler returns to positive free cash flow while holding 2027 capex guidance for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Capacity spending now exceeds operating cash, so buyers raise debt and equity to cover the gap.
rationale: Alphabet funded its quarter with $49.6B of equity and $20.3B of notes and posted its first-ever negative free cash flow, showing the largest buyers turning to outside financing instead of cash.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to capital-market conditions and how long spending outruns cash flow.

falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x perfPerWatt gain over its predecessor.
mechanism: Doing far more compute per megawatt means each scarce unit of power and packaging yields more usable capacity.
rationale: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin racks deliver about ten times the work per megawatt of the prior generation, letting buyers add capacity even where power and packaging are capped.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether each new generation keeps posting large efficiency jumps.

falsifiableTrigger: HBM leadTimes shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for two consecutive quarters before end-2027.
mechanism: Each accelerator needs stacked memory, so when that memory is short it, not the chip, sets how many can ship.
rationale: Micron said its stacked-memory shipments are capped by supply not demand and that this gates NVIDIA and AMD GPU availability, with the shortage running into 2027 and 2028.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast memory makers expand stacked-memory output.

falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margin falls for two consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
mechanism: Scarce memory lets suppliers charge much higher prices, moving profit from server builders to memory makers.
rationale: Micron's data-center memory revenue more than doubled at an 87 percent gross margin and stacked-memory contract prices are set to double, shifting profit toward the memory makers.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory supply catching up and cooling contract prices.

falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 GPUs is announced for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Governments and large enterprises now place clusters big enough to add a new source of accelerator demand.
rationale: A Japanese national project ordered 27,500 Rubin GPUs, an Indonesia factory plans up to 170,000 GPUs, and a large pharma firm is deploying multiple flagship systems, so national and enterprise orders now matter alongside the cloud giants.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to national funding and enterprise AI budgets holding up.

falsifiableTrigger: Intel data-center revenue growth falls below 10% year over year for two consecutive quarters.
mechanism: Rising data-center sales and improving margins bring Intel back as a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
rationale: Intel's data-center and AI revenue grew 59 percent to $6.3B, its gross margin rose to about 40 percent from 27.5 percent, foundry revenue grew 31 percent, and it signed an external foundry customer.
sensitivity: Most sensitive to Intel sustaining product competitiveness and foundry ramp execution.

detail.falsifiableTrigger: New vendor equity-for-compute deals in marginalBuyerFinancing stop appearing for two consecutive quarters.
detail.mechanism: A vendor funds a customer that then commits to buy the vendor's chips, so part of demand depends on the vendor's own money.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these funded customers can pay from their own revenue rather than vendor capital.
detail.statement: Merchant accelerator vendors are now buying equity stakes in the AI firms that buy their chips, tying reported demand to vendor-funded customers beyond NVIDIA alone.
detail.title: chipmakers take equity in their own customers

detail.falsifiableTrigger: Standard DRAM S10 spot prices fall for two consecutive months as suppliers restore non-AI capacity.
detail.mechanism: Memory makers shift capacity to high-margin AI parts, starving other products and driving their prices up.
detail.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much memory capacity stays diverted to AI parts.
detail.statement: The stacked-memory shortage is spreading into standard memory and raising prices on consumer and general-purpose graphics parts.
detail.title: memory crunch spills into consumer and general-purpose parts
